To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Lys324 mutation in the human β1-adrenoceptor generates a receptor that has a single binding site for agonists and a low affinity for the GDP isoform of G protein.

the mutation of Lys324 to Ala in helix 5 of the human β _{1} -AR generated a receptor with a single low-affinity agonist binding site, and this low-affinity binding was converted to high-affinity binding by the addition of the 11-amino acid C-terminal peptide of Gs α.

mutagenesis of a lysine in helix 7 of the human β _{1} -adrenergic receptor generated mutant receptors that have a very low affinity for the GDP bound form of the G protein Gs, and the mutant and wild type β _{1} adrenergic receptor behave differently in assays that determine their proximity to the G protein G _{s}.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the high and low binding sites of agonists to the human β1AR and how the binding sites are regulated by the GDP/GTP-bound state of Gsα.

the molecular mechanisms by which the human β1-adrenoreceptor (β1-AdR) and other G protein-coupling receptors (GPCR), such as the dopamine D2 and the muscarinic m1 receptor, are activated by agonists.
the molecular basis of the high- and low- affinity agonist binding states of the β1-AR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Lys324 residue of the human β _{1} -AR is involved in imparting the high-affinity binding state of agonists.
the high-affinity binding state of the WT receptor is a consequence of the presence of Lys324, and that the low-affinity binding state is a consequence of its absence.
mutagenesis of the β1-AR at position 324 generated a mutant receptor that was unable to form high-affinity binding sites to agonists and had a reduced ability to activate Gs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Lys324 of the human β2- and β1-ARs is involved in the high-affinity binding state of agonists and the GDP-bound Gs isoform.
Lys324 is involved in stabilizing the high-affinity state of agonist-GPCR complexes.
the K324A mutation generates a β1-AR mutant that is defective in the high-affinity binding state for agonist and G protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Lys324 is a residue that is required for the WT β1-adrenerigic receptor to attain its high-affinity state.
the high-affinity binding site for agonists in GPCR is generated by the interaction of agonist-bound GPCRs with the GDP-bound isoforms of G protein.
the high-affinity state of agonist-GPCR interactions is dependent on the interaction between GPCR and the GDP-bound form of G protein.
